rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.e0: In the previous chapter, the black king shut the key squares by standing next to them. Now we will see how to open the way.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.e1: The pawn is on c4, and the key squares are b6, c6 and d6. The black king on c7 stands next to all three.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.e2: To enter a key square the black king is shutting, White uses a tool: the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.e3: Direct opposition: the kings on the same file or rank, with a single square between them. For example, kings on a5 and c5, with b5 between.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.e4: The side that does not have the move has the opposition: the other king must move and give way.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4d5.1: From d5, your king is no longer facing the black king, and Black takes the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4d5.2: The black king goes to d7, facing yours with d6 between them: now Black has the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.c4c5.1: With the pawn on c5, the key squares rise to b7, c7 and d7, and the black king is already on c7.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.c4c5.2: The pawn advanced before the king. The black king goes to c6, right in front of it, and holds the draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4c3.1: From c3, your king is behind the pawn and far from the key squares: Black shuts the way in.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4c3.2: The black king takes c6 and shuts the key squares b6, c6 and d6 to your king.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4d3.1: From d3, your king retreats and does not take the opposition: Black advances and holds the key squares.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4d3.2: The black king takes c6 and shuts the key squares b6, c6 and d6 to your king.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e3.1: From e3, your king moves away from the pawn and the key squares: Black advances and shuts them.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e3.2: The black king takes c6 and shuts the key squares b6, c6 and d6 to your king.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e4.1: From e4, your king is on the pawn's rank but far from the key squares: Black advances and shuts them.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e4.2: The black king takes c6 and shuts the key squares b6, c6 and d6 to your king.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e5.1: From e5, your king gets close to d6 but does not take the opposition: Black advances and shuts the way in.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.err.d4e5.2: The black king takes c6 and shuts the key squares b6, c6 and d6 to your king.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l1: The kings stand face to face, with c6 between them. Black is to move: White has the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l2: Any move by the black king opens the way to a key square.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l3: Zugzwang: being obliged to move when every move worsens the position. If they could pass, Black would stay on c7.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l4: The black king goes to d7 and leaves b6 free.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l5: Your king steps into b6, a key square: the win is guaranteed.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l6: The black king returns to c8, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l7: Your king goes to c6 and takes the opposition again: Black must step out of the way of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l8: The black king goes to d8, and your king goes to b7, next to c8, the promotion square.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l9: Whatever the black king does, the pawn runs to c8 and promotes.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l10: What if the black king went the other way?
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l11: With the black king on b7, d6 is free.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l12: Your king steps into d6, another key square, and the win is still guaranteed.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l13: What if the black king dropped back to c8?
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l14: The black king drops back to c8, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.l15: Your king climbs to c6 and takes the opposition again: the black king must step aside.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! On c5, your king takes the opposition: face to face with the black king, with c6 between them.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to take the king to c5, facing the black king: White has the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing with White and see how Black defends.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.fins.capturado: The black king captured the pawn: it is a draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.fins.afogado: The black king has no move and is not attacked: it is stalemate, and the game is drawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.fins.repeticao: The black king always shut the key squares.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.opposition.ideia.ex1.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.e1: Now let's think from Black's side. The opposition is also a defensive tool.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.e2: The pawn is on e3, and the key squares are d5, e5 and f5. The white king on e4 is already next to all three.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d6.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d6.2: The white king steps into f5, a key square.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d7.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d7.2: The white king steps into e5, a key square, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d8.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7d8.2: The white king steps into e5, a key square, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7e8.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7e8.2: The white king steps into e5, a key square, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f7.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f7.2: The white king steps into e5, a key square, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f8.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f8.2: The white king steps into e5, a key square, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f6.1: With this move, White finds a way to win.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.err.e7f6.2: The white king steps into d5, a key square.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l1: The kings stand face to face, with e5 between them. White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l2: The white king goes to d4 and threatens to enter d5, a key square.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l3: The black king follows to d6 and keeps the opposition: it is the only move.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l3b: Dropping back to e7, it would let the white king into d5.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l4: The pawn advances to e4, and the key squares move up to d6, e6 and f6.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l5: The black king goes to e6, right in front of the pawn: it is the only move. On d7, the white king would take the opposition on d5, and the black king would have to give way.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l6: The pawn advances to e5, and the black king drops back to e7, always in front of it.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l7: The white king goes to d5 and threatens to climb to d6, beside the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l8: The black king takes the opposition again, on d7: it is the only move.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l8b: On d8, e8, f8 or f7, the white king would go to d6 and clear the way for the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l9: The pawn goes to e6, and the black king returns to e7, in front of it.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l10: The white king comes to e5, right behind the pawn, and threatens to go to d6 or f6.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l11: The black king drops back to e8: it is the only move. On d8, the white king would go to d6 and take the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l12: The white king goes to d6 and tries to get past beside the pawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l13: The black king takes the opposition on d8: it is the only move. On f8, the white king would go to d7, and the pawn would promote.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l14: The pawn goes to e7, and the black king returns to e8, in front of it: it is the only move.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l15: The white king goes to e6. The black king cannot go to d7 or f7, next to the white king, nor to d8 and f8, which the pawn attacks.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l16: The pawn is defended, so the black king cannot take it. It is not attacked, yet it has no move.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l17: This is called stalemate: the side to move is not attacked and has no move. The game ends in a draw.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.l18: Here Black had the opposition, and there was no win. With the opposition, the attacker takes the king to the side of the promotion square, as with c5 and b7 in the previous example: that way there is no stalemate.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! On e6, your king takes the opposition and shuts d5, e5 and f5.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to take the king to e6, facing the white king: Black has the opposition.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing with Black and see how White attacks.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.fins.afogado: The black king has no move and is not attacked: it is stalemate, and the game is drawn.
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or tap {verResposta}
rot.opposition.ideia.ex2.p: Black to move. Think and suggest a move, or tap {verResposta}
rot.opposition.demos.retomada.1: A position like the one in the previous chapter: your king is on c5, a key square, and the black king, on d7, is in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.demos.retomada.2: The white king goes to d5 and takes the opposition: it is the only winning move.
rot.opposition.demos.retomada.3: In zugzwang, the black king must step aside and goes to e7. The white king climbs to c6.
rot.opposition.demos.retomada.4: With the king in front, the pawn now climbs to d4 and d5, where the white king protects it.
rot.opposition.demos.retomada.5: The black king returns to d8, in front of the pawn, and the white king takes the opposition on d6.
rot.opposition.demos.retomada.6: The black king steps aside to c8, and the white king goes to e7, next to d8, the promotion square.
rot.opposition.demos.retomada.7: Now the pawn runs to d8 and promotes, with the white king beside it: White wins.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.1: The kings stand face to face, with c4 between them. Black is to move: White has the opposition.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.2: The pawn is on c2, and the key squares are b4, c4 and d4.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.3: It is zugzwang: the black king must move, goes to b5 and leaves d4 free.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.4: The white king steps into d4, a key square.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.5: The black king returns to c6, in front of the pawn.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.6: The white king goes to c4 and takes the opposition: it is the only winning move.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.7a: Let us go back to the previous position, with White to move. What if White advanced the pawn?
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.7: If the pawn advanced to c4, the black king would go to d6, and Black would draw.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.7b: Back to the correct move: with the king on c4, White keeps the opposition and goes on winning.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.11: The black king goes to b6, the white one climbs to d5, and the black one returns to c7, in front of the pawn. The white king takes the opposition on c5.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.12: In zugzwang again, the black king steps aside, and the white king advances to b6.
rot.opposition.demos.vezPretas.curiosida: This position and the next come from the endgame book by Yuri Averbakh (1922–2022), a Soviet grandmaster and one of the greatest endgame experts. Averbakh lived to 100 and was, for a decade, the oldest living grandmaster in the world.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.1: The same position, now with White to move. Let's think from Black's side: Black has the opposition.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.2: The white king goes to b3, heading for b4, a key square.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.3: The black king follows to b5: Black keeps the opposition. It is the only move.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.4: The pawn advances to c4, and the key squares move up to b6, c6 and d6. The black king goes to c5, in front of it.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.6: The white king returns to c3, and the black one drops back to c6. When the white king goes to d4, the black king takes the opposition on d6.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.7: The pawn goes to c5 and attacks the black king on d6, which must leave and drops back to d7.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.9: The white king goes to d5, and the black king returns to c7. The pawn goes to c6, and the black king drops back to c8: it is the only move.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.10: The white king goes to d6, and the black king takes the opposition on d8: it is the only move.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.11: The pawn goes to c7, and the black king returns to c8: it is the only move. On e8, the pawn would promote.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.12: The white king goes to c6: b7 and d7 are next to it, and b8 and d8 are attacked by the pawn.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.13: The black king is not attacked and has no move: it is stalemate, and the game is drawn.
rot.opposition.demos.vezBrancas.14: Same position, the move switched, a different result: whoever has the opposition decides the game.
rot.opposition.demos.longe.1: Now the kings are far apart: the white king is on e4, the pawn on c4, and the kings are not facing each other with a single square between them. Black to move.
rot.opposition.demos.longe.2: The black king goes to e8 and waits on the last rank: if the white king rises to the 5th, it takes the opposition right ahead, on the 7th. It is the only move that draws.
rot.opposition.demos.longe.3: When the white king steps up to e5, the black king takes the opposition on e7: it is the only move.
rot.opposition.demos.longe.4: If the white king goes sideways, to d5, the black king follows, to d7, and keeps the opposition: Black holds the draw.
